solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Destroyed, Miliband trails Right as …

indicators.note: trails means follows behind, so the Miliband piece comes after the other two

parts.note: Ed Miliband, Labour leader until the 2015 election

explanation.surface: A news report on Labour's 2015 defeat: Ed Miliband lags behind the right, a sentence trailing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: RASED is the past tense of RASE, a spelling of RAZE. The ellipsis runs the sentence on into 4 across.
explanation.definitionFit: To rase is to level or demolish a building, so something rased has been destroyed.

clue.text: Write new story on dog fed drug before start of Crufts

indicators.note: the dog is fed, taking the other letters inside it

parts.note: Rover is the traditional name for a dog

indicators.note: the drug letter comes before the next one

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy

indicators.note: the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A Crufts dog-show scandal (a dog poisoned in 2015) prompts a fresh newspaper story.
explanation.walkthrough: Crufts is Britain's famous annual dog show. The definition reads the answer as RE-COVER: write a new cover story about.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as re-cover, it means to cover again, as a journalist covers a story.

clue.text: Crazy twist — Ed (the other one)'s finally lost

parts.note: to screw is to twist

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter, and lost says it goes missing from the surname

parts.note: Ed Balls, the other Labour Ed, who lost his seat in 2015

explanation.surface: A twist in the election story: the other Ed, Ed Balls, finally lost his seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'other' Ed is Ed Balls rather than Ed Miliband. Balls famously lost his seat in 2015.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwball is informal for eccentric or mad, a synonym for crazy.

clue.text: Nursing and changing starts for Charlotte Elizabeth Diana, acclaimed young royal arrival

indicators.note: the letters change places
the first letters of the following words are used

parts.words: Charlotte Elizabeth Diana, acclaimed young royal arrival

explanation.surface: Nappy changes and nursing for Princess Charlotte Elizabeth Diana, the much-welcomed royal baby of 2015.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts for' gives CEDAYRA, and 'changing' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Day care is supervised care for small children, which is a form of nursing them.

clue.text: … leader's character shown in monumental error?

parts.note: a head is a leader, as of a school; the possessive gives HEAD'S
tone is character or quality, as in the tone of a place

explanation.surface: Continuing from 1 across: the Labour leader's character was laid bare by his giant engraved-stone blunder of 2015.
explanation.walkthrough: Miliband's 'EdStone', a tall slab carved with his pledges, was widely mocked as a monumental error, and ED STONE sits inside the answer. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave marker is a monument, and the punning 'monumental error' recalls the much-mocked carved pledge slab.

clue.text: Elevated temperature initially indicated alongside Desmond as things causing floods?

parts.note: high means elevated

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: Des is short for Desmond

explanation.surface: A weather report: a raised temperature recorded along with Storm Desmond, which flooded Cumbria in December 2015.
explanation.walkthrough: Storm Desmond caused severe flooding in northern England. The question mark admits high tides are only one cause of floods.
explanation.definitionFit: Unusually high sea levels at high water can overtop defences and cause flooding.

clue.text: Increasingly smart to have bag, mostly, when coming up to seller? Not half

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from the bottom upwards
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter goes
the first half of the word is not used

explanation.surface: A shopper growing ever more stylish gets a bag from the seller at half price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts BAG to BA, 'coming up' turns it into AB, and 'Not half' leaves LER from SELLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Abler is the comparative of able, meaning cleverer or more capable.

clue.text: Doctor Who's gone to air

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

parts.note: off means gone, as in the milk has gone off

explanation.surface: The Doctor Who star leaves the show and is off the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges WHO'S into SHOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To air one's knowledge is to display it boastfully, which is to flaunt it.

clue.text: Leader of organisation with grim repute

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: dour means grim or severe

explanation.surface: The head of an organisation with a dark reputation, perhaps FIFA's leaders in 2015.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour can mean reputation, as in being in good or bad odour with someone.

clue.text: Towering symbol upholding rudiments of liberty, equality, fraternity France's inhabitants express

indicators.note: in a down clue, upholding means held up, read from the bottom
the rudiments are the first letters of the following words

parts.words: liberty, equality, fraternity France's inhabitants express

explanation.surface: After the 2015 Paris attacks, the French show support for their revolutionary motto at a famous landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rudiments of' gives LEFFIE, and 'upholding' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eiffel Tower is a tall emblem of Paris and of France.

clue.text: Labour leader not for closure in steel town

indicators.note: the closing letter of the surname is not wanted, so it is dropped

parts.note: Jeremy Corbyn became Labour leader in 2015

explanation.surface: The new Labour leader opposes shutting down a steelworks town.
explanation.walkthrough: CORBY is a Northamptonshire town in England famous for its steelworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Corby grew up around its iron and steel industry, making it a classic steel town.

clue.text: Pollster's report wrong? Get out of here!

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the pollster's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Gallup is a well-known polling organisation
off means wrong or mistaken, as in an off note

explanation.surface: The pollsters got the 2015 election badly wrong, and someone tells them to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2015 UK election polls were notoriously wrong. 'report' signals the sound of GALLUP, giving GALLOP.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallop off is to leave at speed, so it works as an order to go away.

clue.text: Assertion from car manufacturer found to be empty?

indicators.note: the carmaker is found to have the empty letter inside it

parts.note: VW is Volkswagen
O, a zero, stands for empty or nothing

explanation.surface: A carmaker's claim turns out to be hollow: a nod to the 2015 Volkswagen emissions scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A vow is a solemn promise or declaration, a firm assertion.

clue.text: America and Cuba entered into reform to restore beginnings of links unexpectedly in about-turn

indicators.note: all the letters are put into a reform, rearranged together

parts.note: C is the international vehicle code for Cuba

indicators.note: the opening letters of two words are taken

explanation.surface: The 2015 thaw in US–Cuba relations: restored links that came as a surprising U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' is the anagram signal; A, C, RESTORE plus L and U are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Changing one's direction or policy is exactly an about-turn.

clue.text: Motorists' hit Top Gear to finish after run

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the run letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: to top is to cut off the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: end means finish

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about the 2015 Top Gear presenter row and the show's ending.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Gear is a BBC motoring show whose presenter Jeremy Clarkson was dropped in 2015. 'Top' removes the G from GEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear-end collision is the bump drivers suffer from the car behind.

clue.text: Deny official EU backing for intervention by leader of Tories

parts.note: a ref, or referee, is a match official

indicators.note: the Tory letter intervenes, coming between the reversed pair
backing means going backwards, so the two letters are turned round
the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A referendum-era headline: the Tory leader steps in, and an official denies backing for the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns EU into UE, and 'intervention by' puts T inside it to give UTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To refute a claim is to deny it or prove it false.

clue.text: Was leaning to the left, formerly in danger of extinction?

indicators.note: formerly means earlier, so the colour comes before the other piece

parts.note: red stands for the political left
listed means leaned over, as a ship lists

explanation.surface: Someone who once leaned to the left is now an endangered species, recalling Labour's 2015 swing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a political turn, but 'formerly' is the placing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Species on the conservation red list are those under threat of dying out.

clue.text: Brassy performer, would-be candidate next year with odds slashed

parts.note: Donald Trump sought the US presidential nomination in 2015

indicators.note: the odd letters are cut out, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A brash showman bidding for next year's election as his betting odds shorten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with odds slashed' removes the odd letters of NEXT YEAR to leave ETER.
explanation.definitionFit: A player on a brass instrument is a brass performer, and brassy also suits the brash candidate.

clue.text: Observe soldiers leaving Yemen after midpoint of ceasefire

indicators.note: the shortened country follows the middle letter
the middle letter of the nine-letter word is taken
the soldiers leave the country's name, so their letters are dropped

parts.note: men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Troops withdraw from Yemen once a truce reaches its halfway point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes MEN out of YEMEN to leave YE.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch or look at it closely.

clue.text: Takes soundings from doctors after further strikes end

indicators.note: the doctors come after the cut word
strikes means knocks out, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: plus means further or in addition
MB is a medical degree, so MBs are doctors

explanation.surface: A medical-staff story: soundings are taken from doctors after more strikes come to an end, recalling the 2015 junior doctors' dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes end' cuts the last letter from PLUS, leaving PLU.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb is to measure water depth with a weighted line, which is taking soundings.

clue.text: Cameron unwinding in Mediterranean island

indicators.note: unwinding untangles the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister relaxes on holiday on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwinding' suggests relaxing but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Menorca is one of the Balearic Islands in the western Mediterranean.

clue.text: Dentist initially is to take Cecil's head on American ship, causing debate

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken
to take means to hold within, so the lion letter is taken in between

parts.note: USS, United States Ship, is the prefix for American naval vessels

indicators.note: the head of a name is where it starts, its opening letter

explanation.surface: The American dentist who killed Cecil the lion in 2015 caused a heated public row.
explanation.walkthrough: Cecil was a famous Zimbabwean lion shot by a US dentist in 2015. 'to take' means the lion's initial is taken in between the two pieces that follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: To discuss something is to talk it over, which is to debate it.

clue.text: Disposed of first of funds after terrible floods

indicators.note: the single letter goes after the rearranged word
terrible means awful, so the letters are badly mangled
the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: After disastrous floods, the first relief money arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges FLOODS into SOLDOF.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell something off is to get rid of it, so sold off means disposed of.

clue.text: With intelligence, we snapped Mars wetly running

indicators.note: running water mixes the letters
snapped means broken off, so these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A NASA team photographs Mars and finds water running there, as announced in 2015.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snapped' takes WE out of WETLY to leave TLY, and 'running' rearranges MARS + TLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To act smartly is to act cleverly, using one's wits.

clue.text: 'Rotten Blatter' — almost habitual response

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Sepp Blatter, the FIFA president ousted in 2015
a tic is a habitual twitch or response

explanation.surface: Calling FIFA's Blatter rotten is almost a reflex reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: A septic wound is infected and putrefying, so septic means rotten.

clue.text: Historic gathering on planet tackling international description of rapid rise

parts.note: ex means former, belonging to history

indicators.note: the rearranged letters tackle, or take hold of, the international letter
the letters are gathered up together in a new order

explanation.surface: The 2015 Paris climate summit, a historic gathering about the planet, tackles fast-rising international problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' rearranges ON PLANET into PONENTAL, and 'tackling' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Exponential growth speeds up ever faster, so the word describes a steep, rapid rise.

clue.text: Element of digital content — photos with lord inhaling drug

indicators.note: inhaling means taking in, so the drug goes inside

parts.note: pix is informal for pictures
L is an abbreviation for lord
E is short for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A tabloid story: pictures of a peer taking drugs, recalling the 2015 Lord Sewel scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pixel is the smallest dot that makes up a digital image.

clue.text: Newspaper boss intervening over revealing pictures

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so everything is read from the bottom
the boss intervenes, coming between the letters

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
ED, short for editor, is the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid editor steps in over topless photos, recalling the Sun's dropping of Page 3 in 2015.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun's Page 3 carried topless photos of models. 'intervening' puts the boss between the first letter and the rest, and 'over' then turns the whole of that upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictures of naked figures reveal all, so nudes are revealing pictures.

clue.text: Whistle-blower will need this as part of appeal

indicators.note: the letters needed form part of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone exposing wrongdoing will need to make an appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: A whistle-blower here is literally someone blowing a whistle, and a referee's whistle has a pea inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The small ball that rattles inside a referee's whistle is called a pea.

clue.text: Payment axed? With critics in majority, revised after short time

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the time letter

parts.note: T is short for time

indicators.note: the letters are revised into a new order
only the majority of the word is used, its last three letters dropped

explanation.surface: The 2015 plan to cut a welfare benefit, dropped after most critics opposed it.
explanation.walkthrough: Tax credits are a UK state top-up for low earners; cuts to them were shelved in late 2015. 'in majority' keeps CRIT, and 'revised' rearranges AXED + CRIT into AXCREDI.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax credit is a benefit sum paid by the state, so it is a kind of payment.

clue.text: Band of Lib Dem MPs?

parts.note: the Liberal Democrats were reduced to eight MPs in 2015, so they would make a musical group of eight

explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight musicians fits the Liberal Democrats' tally of eight seats after the 2015 election.

clue.text: Poor old Special One sacked, having failed

indicators.note: poor means bad or shoddy, so the letters are in a poor, jumbled state
sacked means thrown out, so the letter for one is removed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: José Mourinho, the self-styled Special One, sacked by Chelsea in December 2015 after a failed season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' drops I from SPECIAL, and 'Poor' rearranges SPECAL + OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has collapsed has broken down or fallen through, so it has failed.

clue.text: Transport almost half of refugees heading west on railway

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
the first half of the eight-letter word is taken

explanation.surface: The 2015 migrant crisis: refugees travelling westward by rail and boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' gives REFU, 'almost' leaves REF, and 'heading west' turns it into FER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferry carries people or goods across water, so it is a form of transport.
